In February 1962 President Kennedy banned almost all US trade with Cuba, after Castro's government seized American property. The embargo, which Cubans call the blockade, is still in force.

Laws in 1992 and 1996 tightened it and penalised foreign firms that deal in seized American property. The UN General Assembly has voted against it every year since 1992.

The embargo cut Cuba off from its nearest and largest market and pushed it into trade with the Soviet bloc. After the Special Period and a brief easing under President Obama in 2014 to 2016, it remains a main issue between the two countries and a reason the Cuban government gives for its poverty.
sum: In February 1962 President Kennedy banned almost all US trade with Cuba, after Castro's government seized American property. The embargo, which Cubans call the blockade, is still in force.
